title: Return filing status, late fees and Rule 59(6) restrictions
objective: Verify timely filing of GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-9/9C and other applicable returns and quantify late fee and interest leakages.
procedure:
1. Download the return filing status for all GSTINs for the audit period.
2. Compare filing dates with statutory due dates (including notified extensions) for each return.
3. Recompute late fee for each delayed return and compare with the amount paid through the cash ledger.
4. Check whether GSTR-1 filing was blocked under Rule 59(6) and whether that delayed customer ITC.
5. Record any return not yet filed and the three-year bar on furnishing returns after due date.
expected_result: All returns filed on or before due dates; late fees, if any, correctly paid.
exception_conditions: Returns delayed or unfiled; late fee short-paid; return approaching the three-year filing bar.
exposure_basis: Late fee u/s 47 at notified rates and caps; interest u/s 50(1) on tax paid late; customer disputes from delayed GSTR-1.
evidence_required: Cash ledger extract for late fee debit
corrective_action: File pending returns immediately, pay late fee and interest, and implement a compliance calendar with maker-checker sign-off.

title: All places of business (APOB, warehouses, depots) are registered on the GST certificate
objective: Ensure every location from which goods are supplied, stored or services rendered is declared as principal or additional place of business, so that ITC, e-way bills and books of account are compliant.
procedure:
1. Download the current registration certificate (REG-06) and amendment history for each GSTIN.
2. Compile a list of physical locations from the fixed asset register, rent agreements, electricity/rent ledgers, insurance policies and stock locations in the ERP.
3. Extract dispatch-from and ship-to addresses from the e-way bill register (outward and inward) and compare with registered addresses.
4. Identify unregistered locations, including third-party warehouses, consignment stockists, C&F agents and project sites.
5. For each gap, determine the date the place of business commenced and whether REG-14 was filed within 15 days.
expected_result: Every operating location is reflected in the registration certificate of the correct State GSTIN before commencement of operations.
exception_conditions: Godown or warehouse appearing in e-way bills or stock records but not on REG-06; location in a State without any registration; amendment filed more than 15 days after commencement.
exposure_basis: Penalty u/s 125 (up to Rs 25,000 per contravention) / u/s 122; risk of detention u/s 129 for goods moving from undeclared premises; potential denial of ITC for goods received at unregistered premises; where a new State is involved, tax and interest on supplies made without registration.
evidence_required: Rent/lease agreements and utility bills for each premises
corrective_action: File REG-14 for non-core amendment to add the place of business with supporting documents; obtain new registration where location is in a new State; update ERP location master and e-way bill dispatch addresses.

title: Distinct-person compliance for multi-State GSTINs
objective: Verify that each State registration operates as a distinct person, with inter-unit supplies of goods and services invoiced and taxed under Schedule I.
procedure:
1. List all GSTINs under the PAN and map them to legal entity ledgers and cost centres.
2. Extract inter-branch/stock-transfer ledgers and journal vouchers posting inter-unit charges.
3. Verify that each inter-State stock transfer is supported by a tax invoice (not a delivery challan) with IGST charged and e-way bill generated.
4. Verify that services rendered by HO or one unit to another (management, IT, shared services) are either cross-charged with tax or routed through ISD as applicable.
5. Check valuation of stock transfers against Rule 28 (open market value / 90% of price to unrelated customers at option / invoice value where recipient eligible for full credit).
expected_result: All inter-GSTIN movements and services are invoiced and reported in GSTR-1 of the supplying unit, with matching ITC in the receiving unit.
exception_conditions: Stock transfers on delivery challan; inter-unit services recovered through journal entries without invoice; receiving unit has exempt or non-business supplies but value adopted is nil/arbitrary.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings. Where recipient is fully eligible to ITC, exposure is generally revenue-neutral but interest and penalty remain.
evidence_required: Stock transfer invoices and e-way bills
corrective_action: Raise tax invoices for untaxed inter-unit supplies, pay tax with interest through GSTR-3B/DRC-03, document cross-charge valuation methodology, and configure ERP to block stock transfers without invoice.

title: Validity and status of counterparty GSTINs in vendor and customer masters
objective: Ensure GSTINs used in invoices and ITC claims are structurally valid, active, and belong to the correct legal name and State.
procedure:
1. Run checksum and format validation (15 characters, State code, PAN, entity code, check digit) on all GSTINs in vendor and customer masters and transaction registers.
2. Validate State code of GSTIN against the billing address State in the master.
3. Bulk-verify status (active / suspended / cancelled, with effective dates) and legal name through the GST portal search or GSP API.
4. Flag transactions dated after the cancellation effective date of the counterparty.
5. Check that B2B invoices carry the customer's GSTIN and are not reported as B2C.
expected_result: All GSTINs pass checksum, match PAN and State, and are active on transaction dates.
exception_conditions: Invalid checksum; GSTIN State code differs from address; cancelled/suspended GSTIN on transaction date; legal name mismatch; B2B customer reported without GSTIN.
exposure_basis: ITC on invoices from cancelled/invalid GSTINs reversed with interest u/s 50(3) where utilised; outward supplies reported against wrong GSTIN lead to customer ITC denial and commercial claims.
evidence_required: GSTIN validation report with portal status
corrective_action: Correct masters, amend GSTR-1 records (B2B/B2C reclassification) within the Section 37 time window, stop further payments and ITC on cancelled-vendor invoices, and institute periodic automated GSTIN validation.

title: Timely amendment of registration particulars
objective: Confirm that changes to core and non-core particulars (name, constitution, address, authorised signatories, business activities, bank accounts) are updated within 15 days.
procedure:
1. Obtain board resolutions, ROC filings and HR records for changes in directors, authorised signatories, name or address during the period.
2. Compare current bank accounts used for GST refunds and payments with bank accounts on the registration.
3. Compare principal business activities and HSN/SAC on registration with actual top revenue lines.
4. Check REG-14 filing dates against the change dates.
expected_result: Registration reflects current particulars, with amendments filed within 15 days of each change.
exception_conditions: Former director still listed as authorised signatory; refund bank account not on registration; new business line (e.g., services) not reflected.
exposure_basis: General penalty u/s 125 (up to Rs 25,000); refund processing delays where bank account not validated.
corrective_action: File REG-14 for pending changes; implement a registration change checklist owned by company secretarial and tax teams.

title: Monitoring of vendor suspension and cancellation during the period
objective: Detect vendors whose registration was suspended or cancelled (including retrospective cancellation) so that ITC exposure is identified early.
procedure:
1. Pull registration status for all vendors with purchases above a materiality threshold during the audit period.
2. Identify vendors with cancellation effective dates that precede invoice dates (retrospective cancellation).
3. Check whether ITC from such vendors has been claimed and whether those invoices appear in GSTR-2B.
4. Review vendor payment status and whether the vendor filed GSTR-3B for the relevant periods (GSTR-2A/2B filing status).
5. Evaluate commercial recovery from the vendor (indemnity clauses, retention, withheld payments).
expected_result: No ITC claimed on invoices issued by vendors after their cancellation effective date; risk list maintained for suspended vendors.
exception_conditions: ITC on invoices from retrospectively cancelled vendors; payment released despite vendor non-filing; vendor flagged as non-existent.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Recoverable from vendor where contract permits.
evidence_required: Purchase register extract for affected vendors
corrective_action: Reverse ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) (or 4(B)(1) if permanent), withhold payments, invoke indemnity, and add vendor compliance rating to procurement approval workflow.

title: Sales register vs GSTR-1 reconciliation
objective: Confirm that every outward supply, credit note and debit note recorded in books is reported in GSTR-1/1A in the correct period, table, GSTIN and tax head.
procedure:
1. Reconcile total sales/revenue in the trial balance to the sales register (including other income and FA sales) by GSTIN.
2. Match sales register to GSTR-1/1A at document level using GSTIN + document number + date + taxable value + tax.
3. Classify unmatched items: in books not in GSTR-1, in GSTR-1 not in books, value/tax mismatch, period mismatch, wrong table (B2B vs B2C, export vs domestic).
4. For period mismatches, check whether the later reporting was accompanied by tax payment with interest.
5. Summarise net differences by month and tax head and agree with GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B variance.
expected_result: Document-level match with no unexplained differences; timing items cleared in subsequent periods with interest.
exception_conditions: Invoices missing from GSTR-1; duplicates in GSTR-1; customer GSTIN errors; credit notes reported without corresponding books entry.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
evidence_required: Reconciliation workpaper by GSTIN and month
corrective_action: Report missing documents in the next GSTR-1 or amend through Table 9A/GSTR-1A within the time limit; pay differential tax with interest through GSTR-3B or DRC-03.

title: GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B liability reconciliation
objective: Ensure tax declared in GSTR-1 has been paid through GSTR-3B for each period and head, and anticipate DRC-01B intimations.
procedure:
1. Extract tax liability by head (IGST, CGST, SGST, cess) from GSTR-1 (net of amendments and credit notes) and GSTR-3B Table 3.1 for each month.
2. Compute month-wise and cumulative differences for the financial year.
3. For liability shortfalls in GSTR-3B, identify document-level causes using B-OUT-001 results.
4. Check whether shortfalls were subsequently paid in later GSTR-3B or DRC-03 and whether interest was paid.
5. Check the portal for any DRC-01B intimation and the reply filed (Part B).
expected_result: Cumulative GSTR-3B liability equals or exceeds GSTR-1 liability for each head, with timing differences paid with interest.
exception_conditions: GSTR-1 liability exceeds GSTR-3B without later payment; interest not paid on delayed liability; DRC-01B unanswered.
exposure_basis: Shortfall in tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% from original due date; summary recovery risk u/s 75(12) for self-assessed tax declared in GSTR-1 but not paid.
corrective_action: Pay shortfall with interest via DRC-03 or next GSTR-3B; respond to DRC-01B with reconciliation; correct GSTR-1 where over-reported.

title: Duplicate or non-sequential invoice numbers in sales register
objective: Detect duplicate invoice numbers, re-used series and gaps that may indicate double reporting, suppression or non-compliance with Rule 46.
procedure:
1. Sort sales register by GSTIN, document series and number for each financial year.
2. Identify identical document numbers within the same GSTIN and financial year (case-insensitive, stripping prefixes and spaces).
3. Identify identical customer + date + value combinations under different numbers (potential double booking).
4. Identify gaps in numbering and obtain explanations (cancelled invoices, voided documents) and reconcile with GSTR-1 Table 13.
5. Confirm document numbers do not exceed 16 characters and each series is unique per financial year.
expected_result: Unique consecutive numbering per GSTIN per year; gaps explained by documented cancellations reported in Table 13.
exception_conditions: Duplicate numbers; unexplained gaps; same supply recorded twice; series reset within the year.
exposure_basis: Duplicates may overstate liability (refund/adjustment opportunity) or reflect suppressed supplies (tax + interest + penalty u/s 122). Penalty for incorrect invoices u/s 122.
corrective_action: Cancel or credit-note genuine duplicates, investigate gaps, and enforce system-generated non-editable numbering by GSTIN and year.

title: GST rate applied vs HSN/SAC classification
objective: Verify that the rate charged on each outward supply is consistent with the HSN/SAC and the applicable rate notification at the time of supply.
procedure:
1. Build an item/HSN-to-rate matrix effective date-wise, including rate changes during the period.
2. Compute effective rate per line (tax / taxable value) and compare with the expected rate for the HSN.
3. Flag lines with rate deviations, zero tax on taxable HSN, or multiple rates for the same item in the same period.
4. Review classification of top revenue items with technical literature, product catalogues and any advance ruling.
5. Verify HSN digits reported in GSTR-1 Table 12 meet the minimum digit requirement for the turnover band.
expected_result: Rate per line equals notified rate for the HSN effective on the time of supply; HSN summary consistent with invoices.
exception_conditions: Lower rate charged; inconsistent rates for the same item; rate change not applied from the effective date; HSN digits short.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings. Excess tax charged is generally not refundable where incidence passed on (unjust enrichment).
corrective_action: Pay differential tax with interest, issue supplementary invoices/debit notes where recoverable, correct item master, and obtain classification opinion or advance ruling for disputed items.

title: Correct tax head (IGST vs CGST+SGST) based on place of supply
objective: Ensure inter-State and intra-State classification follows the place of supply rules, particularly for bill-to-ship-to, services and SEZ supplies.
procedure:
1. Derive expected place of supply for each invoice from ship-to/bill-to State (goods) or recipient location and service type (services).
2. Compare supplier State with place of supply to determine expected head; compare with head actually charged.
3. Specifically test supplies to SEZ (must be IGST/zero-rated), bill-to-ship-to across States, and event/immovable property services.
4. For errors, determine whether the customer has taken ITC under the wrong head and the remediation path under Sections 77/19.
5. Check that refunds of wrong-head tax are claimed within the two-year period from date of payment under the correct head.
expected_result: Tax head on every invoice matches the place of supply determination.
exception_conditions: CGST+SGST charged on supply to SEZ or out-of-State ship-to; IGST charged on intra-State supply; POS State in GSTR-1 differs from customer State without justification.
exposure_basis: Tax under the correct head payable in full (no set-off of wrong-head tax); refund of wrong head available u/s 77/IGST s.19 within limitation; no interest on correct-head payment where s.77 applies.
corrective_action: Issue credit note and fresh invoice under the correct head (where customer cooperation available), pay correct tax, file refund of wrong-head tax, and fix POS logic in ERP tax engine.

title: Credit notes issued after Section 34(2) cut-off
objective: Identify credit notes declared after 30 November following the end of the financial year of the original supply (or the annual return date, if earlier) for which output tax has been reduced.
procedure:
1. Extract all credit notes with reference to the original invoice number and date.
2. Determine the financial year of the original supply and the cut-off (30 November following that year, or date of filing GSTR-9 if earlier).
3. Compare credit note GSTR-1 reporting date with the cut-off.
4. For late credit notes, check whether tax was reduced in GSTR-1/GSTR-3B or issued as financial credit notes without GST.
5. Confirm the ERP blocks GST credit notes beyond the cut-off.
expected_result: No reduction of output tax for credit notes beyond the Section 34(2) cut-off; such credit notes issued as commercial/financial credit notes without GST.
exception_conditions: Tax reduced through late credit notes; credit notes without original invoice reference; GSTR-9 filed early, shortening the window.
exposure_basis: Output tax reduced through time-barred credit notes + interest u/s 50(1).
evidence_required: Credit note register with original invoice references
corrective_action: Reverse the tax reduction by paying tax with interest; convert late credit notes to financial credit notes; configure ERP validation on credit note date vs original invoice FY.

title: Credit notes dated before the original invoice or without invoice linkage
objective: Detect credit notes whose date precedes the referenced invoice, or that lack a valid reference, indicating data errors or tax reduction without a valid Section 34 basis.
procedure:
1. Join credit notes to the original invoices on reference number.
2. Flag credit notes where the credit note date is earlier than the original invoice date, or the referenced invoice does not exist in the sales register.
3. Flag credit notes where cumulative credit exceeds original invoice value or tax.
4. Verify the customer GSTIN on the credit note matches the original invoice.
5. Obtain explanation and supporting documentation for each exception.
expected_result: Every credit note references a valid, earlier-dated invoice for the same customer with cumulative credit not exceeding the original.
exception_conditions: Credit note precedes invoice; missing reference; credit exceeds original; GSTIN mismatch.
exposure_basis: Output tax reduced without valid linkage + interest u/s 50(1).
evidence_required: Credit note to invoice mapping report
corrective_action: Correct references through GSTR-1 amendment, reverse ineligible reductions with interest, and enforce mandatory invoice linkage in ERP.

title: Post-supply discounts and credit notes without Section 34 trigger or pre-agreement
objective: Ensure GST is reduced only on credit notes that arise from a Section 34 event (excess value, return, deficiency) and, for discounts, satisfy Section 15(3)(b) including pre-agreement and recipient reversal.
procedure:
1. Classify credit notes by reason code: rate difference, quantity return, quality claim, volume/turnover discount, schemes, price protection, settlement.
2. For discounts, obtain the agreement/scheme circular and verify it existed before or at the time of supply and is linked to specific invoices.
3. Verify that the recipient has reversed ITC: check acceptance on IMS / credit note visibility, or obtain the recipient's certificate (CA/CMA certificate above threshold) as per Circular 212/6/2024-GST.
4. Identify credit notes issued for ad hoc settlements, market support, or claims not pre-agreed and confirm they are issued without GST (financial credit notes).
5. Recompute output tax impact of non-qualifying GST credit notes.
expected_result: GST credit notes only where Section 34/15(3) conditions met with documented pre-agreement and recipient reversal evidence.
exception_conditions: Discount schemes announced after supply; no invoice linkage; recipient ITC reversal not evidenced; recipient rejected credit note on IMS.
exposure_basis: Output tax reduced on non-qualifying credit notes + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18%.
evidence_required: Recipient ITC reversal certificates or IMS acceptance status
corrective_action: Reverse unsupported tax reduction with interest; convert future ad hoc settlements to financial credit notes; obtain recipient certificates contemporaneously.

title: Free-of-cost (FOC) supplies, samples and sales promotion
objective: Ensure FOC supplies are correctly treated: taxable where Schedule I applies (related/distinct persons), ITC reversed where goods are given as gifts/free samples, and delivery documents issued.
procedure:
1. Identify zero-value or FOC lines in the sales register and stock issues to marketing, samples, warranty and promotion cost centres.
2. Classify each FOC movement: related/distinct person supply (Schedule I), gift/free sample to unrelated party, BOGO or bundled offer, warranty replacement.
3. For Schedule I cases, verify tax paid on Rule 28 value.
4. For gifts and free samples to unrelated persons, verify ITC on the inputs/goods has been reversed under Section 17(5)(h).
5. Verify delivery challans/e-way bills accompany FOC movements above threshold.
expected_result: FOC supplies to related/distinct persons taxed; ITC reversed for gifts/samples; promotional bundles priced as composite/mixed supply.
exception_conditions: No tax on FOC supply to group entity; ITC retained on free samples; FOC goods moved without documentation.
exposure_basis: Tax on Schedule I FOC supplies at open-market value + interest; ITC reversal on gifts/samples + interest u/s 50(3) if utilised.
corrective_action: Pay tax on Schedule I FOC supplies, reverse ITC for samples/gifts, and create distinct ERP movement types for samples, gifts and warranty replacements.

title: Advances, unbilled revenue and invoicing within prescribed time
objective: Ensure tax is paid at the correct time of supply on advances for services, and invoices for services are raised within 30 days of supply.
procedure:
1. Extract customer advance ledgers and unbilled revenue/accrued income balances at each month end.
2. For service advances, verify tax paid in the month of receipt and reported in GSTR-1 Table 11A, with adjustment in Table 11B on invoicing.
3. For unbilled revenue, determine the date of completion of service and whether the invoice was raised within 30 days (Rule 47).
4. Compute interest on delayed payment of tax for advances and late invoicing.
5. Confirm advances for goods are excluded (exempted by notification) but correctly identified.
expected_result: Tax on service advances paid in month of receipt; invoices issued within 30 days of completion; unbilled revenue supported by contractual milestones.
exception_conditions: Service advances without tax; unbilled revenue relating to completed services older than 30 days; Table 11 not filed.
exposure_basis: Interest u/s 50(1) for the period of delay on tax relating to advances and late-invoiced services; tax itself if never invoiced.
corrective_action: Pay tax with interest on untaxed advances, report in Table 11A, and implement a monthly unbilled revenue review with tax sign-off.

title: Taxability of other income and miscellaneous recoveries
objective: Identify non-operating income ledgers (scrap sale, recoveries from employees, notice pay, rent, insurance claims, liquidated damages, sale of assets) and confirm correct GST treatment.
procedure:
1. Map every income ledger in the trial balance to its GST treatment (taxable, exempt, non-GST, outside scope).
2. Sample recoveries such as canteen, transport, notice pay, liquidated damages, penalties and insurance claims; examine underlying agreements.
3. Verify that taxable other income has been invoiced and included in GSTR-1/GSTR-3B.
4. Reconcile scrap and sale-of-asset ledgers with tax invoices.
5. Ensure non-taxable receipts are reported appropriately in GSTR-3B/GSTR-9 (exempt/non-GST).
expected_result: Every taxable other-income stream invoiced and taxed; non-GST items supported by analysis.
exception_conditions: Rent, scrap sale or recoveries recognised as income without invoice; liquidated damages treatment undocumented.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Raise invoices and pay tax with interest on taxable income; document positions on non-taxable receipts; route all other income through the billing system.

title: Reporting of exempt, nil-rated and non-GST supplies and linkage to ITC reversal
objective: Ensure exempt and non-GST supplies are correctly reported in GSTR-1 Table 8 and GSTR-3B Table 3.1(c)/(e), and drive common-credit reversal under Rules 42/43.
procedure:
1. Identify exempt, nil-rated and non-GST revenue (e.g., interest income, dividend, sale of land, exempt goods) from the trial balance and sales register.
2. Compare with GSTR-1 Table 8 and GSTR-3B Table 3.1(c)/(e) monthly.
3. Verify the exempt turnover figure used in the Rule 42/43 computations matches the reported figures (including value of securities and land as prescribed).
4. Report differences to C-ITC-008.
expected_result: Exempt/non-GST turnover reported consistently and used in reversal computations.
exception_conditions: Interest/dividend income omitted from exempt turnover; Table 8 blank despite exempt supplies.
exposure_basis: Under-reversal of common credit + interest; reporting inconsistencies triggering ASMT-10.
corrective_action: Correct reporting in subsequent returns and GSTR-9; recompute and reverse common credit.

title: Reimbursements and pure-agent recoveries from customers
objective: Ensure reimbursements recovered from customers (freight, travel, testing, statutory fees) are included in taxable value unless all pure-agent conditions are met.
procedure:
1. Extract reimbursement/recovery ledgers and debit notes raised to customers.
2. Review contracts to determine whether the company acts as pure agent (contractual authorisation, recipient liability, separate disclosure, actual cost).
3. Verify GST charged on recoveries that do not qualify.
4. Check whether recoveries were passed through journal entries without invoices.
expected_result: Non-qualifying reimbursements taxed at the rate of the principal supply; pure-agent recoveries documented.
exception_conditions: Recoveries booked as credits to expense ledgers without invoices; pure agent claimed without contractual support.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Pay tax on non-qualifying recoveries with interest, issue tax invoices, and update contract templates for pure-agent clauses.

title: Purchase register vs GSTR-2B vs GSTR-3B three-way ITC reconciliation
objective: Ensure ITC availed in GSTR-3B is supported by books and reflected in GSTR-2B, and that eligible ITC in GSTR-2B is not lost.
procedure:
1. Reconcile the purchase register (ITC-eligible lines) with GSTR-2B at invoice level for each month (GSTIN + invoice number normalised + date + tax).
2. Classify: matched, in books not in 2B, in 2B not in books, value mismatch, period mismatch, ineligible.
3. Compare total ITC availed in GSTR-3B Table 4(A) for each month with books-eligible and 2B-available ITC.
4. Quantify excess ITC availed over 2B (Rule 36(4)/Section 16(2)(aa) exposure) and unclaimed eligible ITC in 2B.
5. Check for DRC-01C intimations and replies.
expected_result: ITC in GSTR-3B does not exceed eligible ITC appearing in GSTR-2B; unclaimed eligible ITC identified and claimed within Section 16(4) limit.
exception_conditions: ITC claimed on invoices not in GSTR-2B; ITC in 2B not booked; vendor reported under wrong GSTIN; DRC-01C pending.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Unclaimed eligible ITC is an opportunity (E bucket) if within Section 16(4).
corrective_action: Reverse ITC not in 2B (Table 4(B)(2)) and re-claim when reflected; follow up vendors to report; claim missed ITC within time limit; reply to DRC-01C.

title: Duplicate ITC claims on the same invoice
objective: Detect ITC claimed more than once on the same supplier invoice, including across months, GSTINs, or between purchase and expense modules.
procedure:
1. Normalise supplier GSTIN and invoice number (remove prefixes, special characters, leading zeros, FY suffix).
2. Identify duplicate combinations of supplier GSTIN + normalised invoice number + financial year in the purchase register.
3. Identify near-duplicates: same supplier, same date and same tax with different invoice numbers.
4. Check whether duplicates were booked in both AP and expense/journal modules.
5. Quantify duplicate ITC and determine utilisation dates.
expected_result: Each invoice yields ITC only once.
exception_conditions: Same invoice booked twice; invoice booked against two GSTINs; revised invoice claimed alongside original.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse duplicate ITC with interest where utilised, reverse duplicate AP liability, and enforce duplicate-check validation in ERP.

title: ITC claimed after Section 16(4) time limit
objective: Ensure ITC on invoices and debit notes is not availed after 30 November following the end of the financial year of the invoice (or the annual return date, if earlier).
procedure:
1. For each ITC claim, identify the invoice/debit note date and the GSTR-3B period in which ITC was availed.
2. Compute the cut-off: 30 November following the FY of the invoice (for periods before the amendment, the due date of the September return), or GSTR-9 filing date if earlier.
3. For RCM self-invoices, use the FY of the self-invoice date as clarified by Circular 211/5/2024-GST.
4. Flag ITC availed in GSTR-3B filed after the cut-off (consider the filing date, not the return period).
5. For FY 2017-18 to 2020-21, apply Section 16(5) relief for returns filed up to 30.11.2021.
expected_result: No ITC availed beyond the Section 16(4) cut-off.
exception_conditions: Prior-year invoices claimed in December or later; GSTR-3B for October filed late after 30 November; debit notes for old invoices.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse time-barred ITC with interest (if utilised); expense the tax; establish a year-end ITC sweep to claim all prior-year credit by October return.

title: ITC on blocked credits under Section 17(5)
objective: Identify ITC claimed on goods and services blocked under Section 17(5) (motor vehicles, food, health, insurance, club, travel, works contract, construction, gifts, Section 74/129/130 payments).
procedure:
1. Map expense GL codes and HSN/SAC to Section 17(5) categories (e.g., 9963 food, 9993 health, 9971 life/health insurance, 8703 cars, 9954 construction).
2. Extract ITC claimed on mapped ledgers and on capitalised civil/building works.
3. For exceptions (e.g., motor vehicles for specified businesses, obligatory canteen under Factories Act, same-line supplies), obtain supporting evidence.
4. Assess building/civil works for plant-and-machinery treatment considering the Safari Retreats judgment and the retrospective amendment to Section 17(5)(d).
5. Confirm blocked ITC is reported in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(1) where availed from 2B and reversed.
expected_result: No blocked credit retained; exceptions documented.
exception_conditions: ITC on staff welfare/food, car hire, employee insurance, club fees, building construction, Section 74 tax payments.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse blocked ITC in Table 4(B)(1) with interest where utilised; add GL-level blocking rules in ERP.

title: Key-man, life, health and group insurance ITC
objective: Ensure ITC is not claimed on life insurance (including key-man policies), health insurance and group mediclaim unless obligatory under a law in force.
procedure:
1. Extract insurance premium ledgers and classify policies by type: key-man/life, group term life, group health, accident, D&O, property, marine, product liability.
2. For life and health policies, determine whether the cover is obligatory under any statute (e.g., Employees' Compensation Act/ESI exemption conditions) to fall within the proviso.
3. Key-man insurance (life insurance on the life of key person for company's benefit) — confirm ITC reversed as blocked under Section 17(5)(b)(i).
4. Confirm ITC on business-risk insurances (property, marine, D&O liability) is retained.
expected_result: ITC claimed only on insurance that is not blocked or is obligatory under law.
exception_conditions: ITC on key-man, group mediclaim or group term life premiums without statutory obligation.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse ineligible insurance ITC with interest where utilised; tag insurance types in AP for automatic blocking.

title: Rule 37 reversal for non-payment to suppliers within 180 days
objective: Ensure ITC is reversed where value plus tax is not paid to the supplier within 180 days of the invoice date, and re-availed on payment.
procedure:
1. Obtain AP ageing as on each month end with invoice-level detail and tax component.
2. Identify invoices outstanding beyond 180 days (including partial payments, retention money, disputed invoices).
3. Exclude deemed-paid items (e.g., RCM, specified deemed supplies without consideration).
4. Verify reversal in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) in the period following the 180th day and re-claim after payment in Table 4(A)(5).
5. Assess interest where ITC reversed late (Section 50(3), only if utilised).
expected_result: Reversals made for all invoices crossing 180 days unpaid; re-claims supported by payments.
exception_conditions: Retention money/withheld amounts not reversed; disputed invoices ignored; re-claim before payment.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Temporary reversal; re-available on payment (E bucket).
corrective_action: Reverse ITC on overdue payables, track for re-claim, and automate a 180-day AP report linked to GST reversal.

title: Rule 37A reversal where supplier has not filed GSTR-3B
objective: Ensure ITC on invoices reported in GSTR-1 by suppliers who have not filed GSTR-3B by 30 September following the year end is reversed by 30 November.
procedure:
1. Download GSTR-2B for each month and identify supplier records flagged with GSTR-3B non-filing (Rule 37A advisory section) and supplier filing status from GSTR-2A.
2. Quantify ITC availed from suppliers who had not filed GSTR-3B for the relevant period as on 30 September.
3. Verify reversal in GSTR-3B on or before 30 November and re-claim upon subsequent supplier filing.
4. Engage with procurement to withhold payments to non-compliant vendors.
expected_result: Rule 37A reversals timely made and tracked for re-claim.
exception_conditions: ITC retained despite supplier non-filing; reversal made after 30 November.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse ITC with interest where applicable; re-claim when supplier files; incorporate supplier filing status in payment release.

title: Common credit reversal under Rules 42 and 43 (exempt and non-business use)
objective: Verify monthly and annual reversal of common ITC attributable to exempt supplies and non-business use.
procedure:
1. Classify ITC into T1 (non-business), T2 (exclusively exempt), T3 (blocked) and common credit C2 for inputs/input services; identify common capital goods for Rule 43.
2. Compute exempt turnover ratio (including exempt and non-taxable supplies as prescribed) for each month and the year.
3. Recompute monthly D1/D2 reversals and the annual true-up; compare with reversals in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(1).
4. Compute Rule 43 monthly reversal for common capital goods over 60 months.
5. Compute interest on short reversal from April following the year end as per Rule 42(2).
expected_result: Monthly provisional and annual final reversals correctly computed and reported.
exception_conditions: No reversal despite exempt income (e.g., interest, sale of land, exempt services); annual true-up not done.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Interest per Rule 42(2)/43 on short reversal.
corrective_action: Reverse short computed credit with interest and institutionalise a monthly Rule 42/43 working signed off by tax.

title: ITC from cancelled, suspended or invalid GSTINs
objective: Detect ITC availed on invoices from suppliers whose GSTIN was invalid, cancelled or suspended on the invoice date.
procedure:
1. Run GSTIN validation on all purchase register lines carrying ITC.
2. Match invoice dates with supplier cancellation effective dates.
3. Quantify ITC on invalid/cancelled GSTINs and check its presence in GSTR-2B.
4. Check if any Rule 86A blocking has been imposed on the electronic credit ledger.
expected_result: No ITC from invalid or cancelled GSTINs.
exception_conditions: ITC on invoices with typo GSTINs or from cancelled suppliers; ledger blocked under Rule 86A.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
evidence_required: GSTIN status report for purchase lines
corrective_action: Reverse ineligible ITC, recover tax from vendor, correct vendor master, and pursue unblocking with documents where ITC is genuine.

title: Invoice Management System actions (accept, reject, pending)
objective: Ensure IMS actions on inward records are deliberate and consistent with books, so GSTR-2B reflects only valid ITC and credit notes.
procedure:
1. Download IMS data for each period with action status (accepted, rejected, pending, deemed accepted).
2. Match IMS records with purchase register; ensure records not in books (or disputed) are rejected or kept pending with justification.
3. Ensure credit notes from suppliers are not rejected merely to avoid ITC reduction where the credit note is genuine.
4. Verify pending records are reviewed before the time limit for ITC and that GSTR-2B is recomputed after late actions.
5. Document approval matrix for IMS actions.
expected_result: IMS actions consistent with books; no blanket deemed acceptance of records not in books.
exception_conditions: Records accepted though goods/services not received; genuine supplier credit notes rejected; large pending volumes near cut-off.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Rejecting a valid supplier credit note may lead to ITC reduction demands.
corrective_action: Rectify IMS actions before 2B generation, recompute GSTR-2B where permitted, and implement a weekly IMS review routine.

title: ITC reduction on credit notes received from suppliers
objective: Ensure ITC is reduced for credit notes issued by suppliers (returns, discounts, rate revisions) and accounted in books.
procedure:
1. Extract supplier credit notes from GSTR-2B/IMS (B2B-CDNR).
2. Match with debit notes/credit notes booked in purchase register and journal vouchers.
3. Identify credit notes in GSTR-2B not booked and verify ITC reduction in GSTR-3B.
4. Identify volume rebates/discounts received as financial credit notes and confirm no ITC impact required.
expected_result: ITC reduced for all supplier credit notes in GSTR-2B.
exception_conditions: Supplier credit notes not booked; ITC not reduced; rebates received without supplier credit note where GST impact intended.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse ITC for unbooked supplier credit notes with interest where utilised and include CDNR matching in monthly close.

title: Receipt of goods/services condition and bill-to-ship-to
objective: Ensure ITC is claimed only after goods or services are received (including deemed receipt in bill-to-ship-to) and on the last lot for multiple-lot supplies.
procedure:
1. Compare invoice date, GRN date and ITC claim period for sample invoices and for all high-value invoices.
2. Identify invoices booked at period end with GRN in the following period.
3. For bill-to-ship-to, verify e-way bills show delivery to the third party on the company's direction.
4. For services, obtain evidence of service rendering (reports, timesheets, deliverables).
expected_result: ITC claimed in the period of receipt with documentary proof.
exception_conditions: ITC claimed before GRN; no evidence of service receipt; e-way bill shows delivery elsewhere without direction.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A. Penalty u/s 122 for availing ITC without receipt.
corrective_action: Defer/reverse ITC to the period of receipt, link ITC claim to GRN in ERP.

title: Shipping-line, CHA and freight-forwarder invoices for FTWZ/warehoused consignments
objective: Ensure ITC on shipping line, CHA and logistics invoices relating to goods held in FTWZ or customs warehouses is claimed only by the correct recipient GSTIN and only where the services relate to taxable/zero-rated supplies of the claimant.
procedure:
1. Extract invoices from shipping lines, CFS, CHA and freight forwarders and map each to the import consignment (BL/BOE number).
2. Identify consignments landed into FTWZ/SEZ units or customs bonded warehouses and their subsequent disposal (DTA clearance by the company, sale while warehoused, re-export).
3. Verify invoices are in the name and GSTIN of the company (not the FTWZ unit) and that the services were received by the company.
4. Where goods are sold while in FTWZ/warehouse (Schedule III para 8(a)), evaluate whether ITC on attributable services requires reversal as related to non-supply (Rule 42).
5. Where FTWZ unit is the recipient, confirm charges should have been zero-rated to the SEZ unit and not claimed as ITC in DTA.
expected_result: ITC on logistics charges claimed only where the company is the recipient and the goods feed taxable or zero-rated supplies.
exception_conditions: ITC claimed on charges billed to FTWZ unit; ITC retained on services linked to warehoused sales outside GST; IGST charged by shipping line on SEZ-bound services.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Reverse ineligible ITC, request corrected invoices (correct GSTIN/zero-rating) from vendors, and define consignment-level ITC coding for FTWZ flows.

title: GSTR-3B Table 4 reporting and Electronic Credit Reversal and Re-claimed Statement (ECRRS)
objective: Ensure permanent and temporary ITC reversals are reported in the correct tables and re-claims do not exceed the reversed balance in ECRRS.
procedure:
1. Extract GSTR-3B Table 4(A), 4(B)(1), 4(B)(2), 4(D)(1) and 4(D)(2) for each month.
2. Reconcile temporary reversals (Rule 37, 37A, 16(2)(b)/(c)) to ECRRS opening balance and closing balance.
3. Verify re-claims in 4(A)(5)/4(D)(1) are supported by documentation and do not exceed ECRRS balance.
4. Check that permanent reversals are not re-claimed.
expected_result: ECRRS balance equals temporarily reversed ITC pending re-claim; table-wise reporting correct.
exception_conditions: Re-claim exceeding ECRRS balance; permanent reversals reported in 4(B)(2); opening ECRRS balance not declared.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Correct reporting prospectively, reverse unsupported re-claims, and maintain a reversal/re-claim register.

title: ITC mismatch for FY 2017-18 and 2018-19 (GSTR-2A vs GSTR-3B)
objective: Quantify and defend ITC claimed for FY 2017-18 and 2018-19 not reflected in GSTR-2A using the Circular 183/15/2022-GST procedure.
procedure:
1. Reconcile purchase register with GSTR-2A (as GSTR-2B did not exist) for FY 2017-18 and 2018-19.
2. Classify mismatches: supplier did not file, supplier filed under wrong GSTIN/B2C, filed in later period.
3. For each supplier above the Circular threshold, obtain a CA/CMA certificate; below threshold, supplier certificate confirming supply and tax payment.
4. Map to any pending notices/orders for these years and limitation status.
expected_result: All mismatches supported by certificates per Circular 183/15/2022.
exception_conditions: Certificates not obtained; supplier non-filer; mismatch already confirmed in order.
exposure_basis: Ineligible/excess ITC to be reversed + interest u/s 50(3) @ 18% p.a. only to the extent the credit was utilised (electronic credit ledger balance fell below the wrongly availed amount, Rule 88B); penalty exposure u/s 73/74/74A.
corrective_action: Collect certificates, file replies, and pay where unsupported (consider Section 128A waiver eligibility).

title: RCM on notified services (GTA, legal, directors, security, sponsorship, motor vehicle renting)
objective: Ensure tax under reverse charge is discharged on all services notified under Section 9(3).
procedure:
1. Map expense ledgers and vendor categories to notified RCM services: GTA (where supplier has not opted forward charge), advocate/legal fees, director sitting fees and remuneration (non-employee), security services by non-body corporate, sponsorship, renting of motor vehicles by non-body corporate (where conditions apply), insurance agent, recovery agent services.
2. Extract total payments/expenses per category per month and recompute RCM liability.
3. Compare with RCM paid in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) and with self-invoices issued.
4. For GTA, verify vendor declarations of forward charge option.
5. Confirm ITC on RCM paid availed in Table 4(A)(3).
expected_result: RCM liability paid in cash in the month of time of supply for all notified services.
exception_conditions: No RCM on director sitting fees or legal fees; GTA under RCM treated as forward charge without declaration; RCM paid late.
exposure_basis: RCM tax payable in cash + interest u/s 50(1) from time of supply; ITC re-available (largely revenue-neutral except interest and blocked/ exempt-use portions).
corrective_action: Pay RCM with interest through DRC-03 or next GSTR-3B, issue self-invoices, claim ITC in the period of payment, and configure RCM tax codes in vendor master.

title: IGST under reverse charge on import of services
objective: Ensure IGST is paid on all services received from suppliers located outside India where the place of supply is India.
procedure:
1. Extract foreign currency outward remittances (Form 15CA/CB data, bank SWIFT records) and foreign vendor ledgers.
2. Classify each payment: import of goods, import of services, reimbursement, capital transaction.
3. Determine place of supply under IGST Section 13 for each service.
4. Compare IGST RCM payable with GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) by month (time of supply per Section 13(3) including associated enterprise rule).
5. Verify ITC on RCM paid claimed in Table 4(A)(2).
expected_result: IGST paid on all imported services in the correct period.
exception_conditions: Royalty, consultancy, software, marketing, commission paid abroad without RCM; RCM paid on payment date ignoring AE book entry date.
exposure_basis: IGST under RCM + interest u/s 50(1); ITC generally re-available, so exposure is primarily interest and penalty except where ITC restricted.
corrective_action: Pay IGST with interest, claim ITC, and include GST RCM check in the foreign remittance approval workflow.

title: Foreign software, SaaS and online subscriptions paid by corporate cards
objective: Capture import of services paid through corporate credit cards and employee reimbursements (cloud, SaaS, advertising, subscriptions) for RCM.
procedure:
1. Extract corporate card statements and employee expense claims with foreign currency transactions.
2. Identify foreign vendors (cloud services, design tools, ads platforms, journals, conferences).
3. Check whether the vendor issued an invoice with Indian GSTIN (forward charge as OIDAR supplier to registered persons is not applicable; registered recipient pays RCM).
4. Recompute IGST RCM and compare with RCM paid.
expected_result: RCM paid on all foreign digital services received by the registered entity.
exception_conditions: Card spends on foreign SaaS without RCM; vendor invoices addressed to employees.
exposure_basis: IGST under RCM + interest u/s 50(1).
corrective_action: Pay IGST RCM with interest, update vendor invoices to company GSTIN where available, and route subscriptions through AP.

title: Recharges and reimbursements to overseas group entities
objective: Ensure cost allocations, management fees, recharges and reimbursements payable to overseas related parties are evaluated as import of services, including transactions without consideration.
procedure:
1. Obtain intercompany agreements, transfer pricing documentation and intercompany ledger entries with overseas group entities.
2. Identify cost allocations (IT, HR, insurance, licences, travel) and reimbursements of costs incurred abroad on behalf of the Indian entity.
3. Determine whether each is a supply of service by the overseas entity; where no consideration, evaluate Schedule I para 4.
4. Apply valuation: invoice value deemed OMV where Indian entity eligible for full ITC (Circular 210/4/2024-GST); otherwise Rule 28.
5. Determine time of supply for associated enterprises (earlier of book entry and payment) and compare with RCM paid.
expected_result: RCM paid on all taxable intercompany services at correct value and time.
exception_conditions: Recharges booked via journal entries without RCM; time of supply based only on payment; partial-exempt entity adopting nil value.
exposure_basis: IGST RCM + interest u/s 50(1) from book-entry date; ITC restricted where entity has exempt supplies.
corrective_action: Pay RCM with interest, issue self-invoices, align GST with transfer pricing documentation, and set an intercompany RCM review at each book closing.

title: Directors' and officers' insurance or employee benefits paid abroad by parent and recharged
objective: Ensure premiums for D&O liability, global health or life policies taken by the overseas parent and recharged to the Indian entity are assessed for RCM and blocked-credit treatment.
procedure:
1. Identify global insurance programmes (D&O, global medical, group life) where premium is allocated to the Indian entity.
2. Determine the service provider (foreign insurer or parent) and whether a supply is made to the Indian entity.
3. Compute RCM on recharged amount (or OMV) and assess ITC: D&O liability cover generally eligible; health/life cover blocked unless obligatory.
4. Verify RCM paid and ITC treatment.
expected_result: RCM discharged on taxable recharges with correct ITC treatment.
exception_conditions: Global insurance recharge with no RCM; ITC claimed on blocked health/life component.
exposure_basis: IGST RCM + interest; blocked ITC reversal + interest u/s 50(3) where utilised.
corrective_action: Pay RCM with interest, reverse blocked ITC, and document allocation basis.

title: Warranty claims, replacements and reimbursements — GST character
objective: Determine the GST treatment of warranty claims paid to dealers, service centres or overseas parties, and of replacement parts supplied under warranty.
procedure:
1. Extract warranty expense and claim ledgers and identify payees (domestic dealers, overseas distributors, service centres, customers).
2. For domestic dealers, verify dealer invoices with GST for repair labour/parts and ITC eligibility.
3. For overseas parties, determine whether services are performance-based on goods located outside India (place of supply outside India under IGST Section 13(3)) or other services with place of supply in India (RCM).
4. For replacement parts supplied free under warranty, apply Circular 195/07/2023-GST (no tax, no ITC reversal for manufacturer); verify extended warranty is taxed separately.
5. Check credit notes to customers labelled as warranty for Section 34 eligibility.
expected_result: Warranty transactions treated per their character, with RCM paid only where place of supply is India.
exception_conditions: Payments to overseas service providers without POS analysis; ITC reversed unnecessarily on warranty replacements; extended warranty not taxed.
exposure_basis: IGST RCM + interest where POS in India; potential refund/ITC opportunity where reversal not required.
corrective_action: Pay RCM where applicable, re-avail ITC wrongly reversed (within Section 16(4) limits), and document warranty GST policy.

title: RCM on notified goods and Section 9(4) supplies
objective: Ensure reverse charge is paid on notified goods and, where the taxpayer falls within notified classes (e.g., real-estate promoters), on supplies from unregistered persons.
procedure:
1. Identify purchases of notified RCM goods by HSN from the purchase register.
2. Determine whether the taxpayer is a notified class under Section 9(4) and quantify purchases from unregistered suppliers.
3. Recompute RCM and compare with Table 3.1(d).
4. Verify self-invoices and payment vouchers.
expected_result: RCM paid on notified goods and applicable unregistered purchases.
exception_conditions: Notified goods purchased without RCM; promoter shortfall in purchases from registered suppliers not taxed.
exposure_basis: RCM tax + interest u/s 50(1).
corrective_action: Pay RCM with interest and add HSN-based RCM flags in item master.

title: Self-invoices, payment vouchers and time of supply for RCM
objective: Verify issuance of self-invoices and payment vouchers and correct determination of time of supply for RCM transactions.
procedure:
1. Obtain the self-invoice series and payment vouchers for the period.
2. Match RCM transactions with self-invoices and check dates relative to receipt of supply (Rule 47 time limit applies for self-invoices).
3. Recompute time of supply (payment date / 60 days from supplier invoice / AE book entry) and compare with RCM payment period.
4. Compute interest for delayed RCM payment.
expected_result: Self-invoice issued for every RCM purchase from unregistered supplier within time; RCM paid in correct period.
exception_conditions: No self-invoices; RCM paid on annual basis; delayed self-invoicing used to extend Section 16(4) window.
exposure_basis: Interest u/s 50(1) on delayed RCM; penalty u/s 122/125 for non-issuance of documents.
corrective_action: Issue self-invoices contemporaneously, pay interest, and automate RCM document generation.

title: RCM paid in cash and corresponding ITC claimed
objective: Verify RCM liability is discharged only through the electronic cash ledger and that ITC on RCM paid is claimed once in the correct period.
procedure:
1. Compare RCM liability in Table 3.1(d) with cash ledger debits for each period.
2. Compare RCM ITC claimed in Table 4(A)(2)/(3) with RCM paid and with the portal RCM liability/ITC statement where available.
3. Identify RCM ITC claimed without payment or in excess.
4. Identify RCM paid but ITC not claimed (opportunity within Section 16(4)).
expected_result: RCM ITC equals eligible RCM paid in cash.
exception_conditions: RCM liability set off against ITC; RCM ITC claimed without payment; RCM ITC missed.
exposure_basis: Tax re-payable in cash where set off against credit + interest; ITC over-claim reversal + interest u/s 50(3).
corrective_action: Pay RCM in cash, reverse unsupported RCM ITC, and claim missed RCM ITC.

title: RCM on renting of commercial property from unregistered landlords
objective: Ensure reverse charge is paid on renting of immovable property (other than residential dwelling) by an unregistered person to a registered person, as notified with effect from 10.10.2024.
procedure:
1. Extract rent ledgers and landlord master data with GST registration status.
2. Identify commercial premises rented from unregistered landlords on or after 10.10.2024.
3. Recompute RCM and verify payment and self-invoice.
4. Exclude composition-registered landlords only if specifically excluded as per the amended entry; document conclusion.
expected_result: RCM paid on all applicable rent payments from 10.10.2024.
exception_conditions: Rent from unregistered landlords without RCM.
exposure_basis: RCM tax + interest u/s 50(1).
corrective_action: Pay RCM with interest and add landlord GST status to lease management.

title: Ocean freight and transportation services on imports
objective: Ensure IGST under RCM is not paid on ocean freight for CIF imports post Mohit Minerals, and that freight arrangements on FOB/EXW terms are evaluated under place-of-supply rules.
procedure:
1. Classify imports by Incoterm and identify who contracted the ocean freight.
2. For CIF imports, check whether RCM was paid on ocean freight and whether refund was claimed within limitation.
3. For FOB/EXW imports where the company contracts with a foreign or Indian freight provider, determine taxability and place of supply.
4. Verify GST charged by Indian freight forwarders and ITC eligibility.
expected_result: No RCM on CIF ocean freight; correct treatment for other freight contracts.
exception_conditions: RCM continuing on CIF imports; refund not pursued; FOB freight from foreign shipping lines untreated.
exposure_basis: Refund opportunity for RCM wrongly paid (subject to limitation and unjust enrichment); RCM + interest where FOB freight is taxable in India.
corrective_action: Stop RCM on CIF freight, file refund where within time, and document freight GST positions.

title: Mandatory ISD registration for common input services
objective: Ensure that an office receiving invoices for common input services on behalf of distinct persons is registered as ISD from 01.04.2025.
procedure:
1. List all GSTINs under the PAN and identify the office (usually HO) receiving invoices for services consumed by multiple units (audit fees, IT, advertisement, insurance, consultancy).
2. Verify ISD registration exists in each State where such invoices are received.
3. Identify common-service invoices received in a normal GSTIN after 01.04.2025.
4. Evaluate exposure where credit retained in a single GSTIN instead of distributed.
expected_result: ISD registration obtained and common services invoiced to ISD GSTIN.
exception_conditions: No ISD registration; common invoices booked in normal GSTIN.
exposure_basis: ITC on common services retained in a single GSTIN may be challenged; general penalty exposure under the Act; working capital loss in units.
corrective_action: Obtain ISD registration, update vendor billing GSTIN, and distribute credit through GSTR-6.

title: ISD distribution as per Rule 39
objective: Verify that ISD credit is distributed in the same month, to the correct recipients, on turnover ratio, with matching heads.
procedure:
1. Download GSTR-6 and ISD-received GSTR-6A/2B for each month.
2. Verify all credit received is distributed in the same month.
3. Recompute distribution ratio based on turnover of recipient units for the prescribed period.
4. Verify head-wise distribution (IGST to other States, CGST/SGST to same State) and ineligible credit distributed as ineligible.
expected_result: Complete, timely and correctly apportioned distribution.
exception_conditions: Undistributed balance; distribution to units not using the service; wrong ratio; ineligible credit distributed as eligible.
exposure_basis: Excess credit distributed recoverable from recipients with interest; under-distribution leads to lost ITC.
corrective_action: Issue ISD credit notes/supplementary invoices to correct distribution and standardise distribution keys.

title: ISD distribution reflected in GSTR-2B but not booked by recipient units
objective: Ensure ISD credit distributed to recipient units is recorded in their books and availed in GSTR-3B.
procedure:
1. Extract ISD section of each recipient unit's GSTR-2B.
2. Match with ISD invoices booked in the unit's purchase register/journal.
3. Identify unbooked distributions and evaluate time limit for claiming.
4. Confirm GSTR-3B Table 4(A)(4) reporting.
expected_result: All ISD distributions booked and claimed by recipients.
exception_conditions: ISD credit in 2B not booked; claimed late beyond Section 16(4).
exposure_basis: Lost ITC (opportunity) if not claimed within time limit.
corrective_action: Book and claim ISD credit, and add ISD 2B review in unit monthly close.

title: Common-service vendors billing normal GSTIN instead of ISD or consuming unit
objective: Identify vendors invoicing common services to a normal GSTIN where services are consumed by other units, which distorts ITC and may breach ISD requirements.
procedure:
1. Identify vendors whose services benefit multiple locations (telecom, IT, audit, advertising, security for multiple sites).
2. Check billing GSTIN on their invoices vs consuming locations (cost centre mapping).
3. Quantify ITC claimed by HO GSTIN for services consumed in other States.
4. Evaluate correction: re-billing to ISD or to consuming GSTIN; or cross-charge.
expected_result: Common services billed to ISD; location-specific services billed to the consuming unit.
exception_conditions: Out-of-State site services billed to HO GSTIN; common services not distributed.
exposure_basis: ITC claimed by non-recipient GSTIN may be disallowed + interest u/s 50(3) where utilised.
corrective_action: Instruct vendors to bill ISD/consuming unit, cross-charge where appropriate, and update vendor master billing GSTIN.

title: Cross-charge of head office services to branches
objective: Ensure supplies of services by HO to branches (distinct persons) are identified, valued and taxed or properly concluded upon.
procedure:
1. Identify HO functions supporting branches (management, finance, HR, IT, procurement).
2. Review cross-charge invoices issued and valuation methodology.
3. Where branches are eligible for full ITC, document adoption of invoice value as OMV per Circular 199/11/2023; where branches make exempt supplies, compute cost-based value under Rule 28 (salary costs need not be included as clarified).
4. Verify reporting of cross-charge invoices in GSTR-1 and ITC in branches.
expected_result: Documented cross-charge policy consistent with Circular 199/11/2023.
exception_conditions: No cross-charge where branches have exempt supplies; cross-charge invoices not reported.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Adopt and document a cross-charge policy and pay tax with interest where branches are not fully eligible.

title: Employee secondment and shared employees between GSTINs
objective: Evaluate GST treatment of employees of one GSTIN working for another (secondment, shared services) including salary recharges.
procedure:
1. Identify salary cost recharges between units from payroll cost-centre allocations and journals.
2. Determine whether recharge reflects supply of services by distinct person.
3. Apply Circular 199/11/2023 for valuation and recipient ITC eligibility.
4. Verify invoicing and GSTR-1 reporting where taxed.
expected_result: Salary recharges evaluated and taxed or documented.
exception_conditions: Salary recharges via journals with no GST analysis.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Document position and invoice where required.

title: E-invoice register vs GSTR-1 vs books
objective: Ensure every IRN generated is recorded in books and auto-populated in GSTR-1, and that cancelled IRNs are not reported.
procedure:
1. Download IRN register from IRP/e-invoice portal (active and cancelled).
2. Match IRNs with sales register (document number, date, value, GSTIN).
3. Match IRNs with GSTR-1 auto-populated data and identify overwritten/edited records.
4. Classify: IRN active not in books, in books without IRN, cancelled IRN in books/GSTR-1, value mismatch.
expected_result: Three-way match with no unexplained items.
exception_conditions: IRN generated but invoice not booked or not in GSTR-1; cancelled IRN still in books; GSTR-1 record edited post auto-population.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Book or cancel orphan IRNs, correct GSTR-1, and pay tax with interest on unreported active IRNs.

title: B2B invoices, credit/debit notes and exports without IRN
objective: Identify documents required to be e-invoiced that were issued without IRN, which are not valid invoices under Rule 48(5).
procedure:
1. Confirm e-invoice applicability based on AATO of any FY from 2017-18 onwards.
2. Filter sales register for B2B, SEZ, export and B2B credit/debit note documents.
3. Match to IRN register; list documents without IRN.
4. Check for exempt categories (e.g., exempt supplies, RCM-only documents).
expected_result: All in-scope documents carry valid IRN and QR code.
exception_conditions: B2B invoices without IRN; credit notes without IRN; manual invoices from branches.
exposure_basis: Invoice not valid → customer ITC denial and commercial claims; penalty u/s 122; detention risk in transit (s.129).
corrective_action: Generate IRN where permissible within time limits, else cancel and re-issue; block invoice printing without IRN in ERP.

title: E-invoices generated but missing or amended in GSTR-1
objective: Detect active IRNs not reported in GSTR-1 (e.g., auto-population failures, deletions) and resulting liability shortfalls.
procedure:
1. Compare active IRN list for each month with GSTR-1 B2B/EXP/SEZ and CDNR tables.
2. Identify records deleted from GSTR-1 auto-draft before filing.
3. Assess liability impact and DRC-01B risk.
expected_result: All active IRNs reported in GSTR-1 of the correct period.
exception_conditions: Active IRNs deleted from GSTR-1; IRNs generated for a different GSTIN.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings.
corrective_action: Report missing IRNs and pay tax with interest; restrict deletion rights in GSTR-1 preparation.

title: 30-day reporting limit for IRN generation
objective: Ensure IRN generation within 30 days of document date for notified AATO classes.
procedure:
1. Compute lag between document date and IRN acknowledgement date for each document.
2. Flag documents with lag beyond 30 days and those rejected by IRP for this reason.
3. Determine how rejected documents were handled (re-dated, issued without IRN).
expected_result: IRNs generated promptly, well within 30 days.
exception_conditions: Backdated invoices; credit notes not e-invoiced due to lapse; re-dating to circumvent restriction.
exposure_basis: Invalid documents leading to customer ITC denial; liability timing errors + interest.
corrective_action: Enforce real-time IRN generation and monitor lag weekly.

title: E-invoice applicability assessment across PAN
objective: Verify the entity's e-invoice applicability considering AATO across all GSTINs under the PAN for each FY since 2017-18, and any exempt class status.
procedure:
1. Compute AATO for each FY from 2017-18 using PAN-level turnover.
2. Compare with thresholds and their effective dates.
3. Check claimed exemption status (SEZ unit, bank, insurer, GTA, passenger transport, multiplex).
expected_result: Applicability correctly determined and implemented from the right date.
exception_conditions: E-invoicing not started on crossing threshold; SEZ developer wrongly assuming exemption.
exposure_basis: All B2B invoices since applicability date invalid → customer ITC risk and penalties.
corrective_action: Commence e-invoicing immediately and assess remediation for past invoices.

title: Supply type, POS and HSN in e-invoices for exports, SEZ and RCM
objective: Verify e-invoice supply type codes (B2B, SEZWP, SEZWOP, EXPWP, EXPWOP, DEXP), reverse charge flag, POS and HSN accuracy.
procedure:
1. Extract e-invoice JSON fields for supply type, POS, port code, shipping bill and HSN.
2. Compare supply type with nature of supply in books (with/without payment of tax).
3. Verify LUT-based supplies are coded WOP and taxed supplies WP.
4. Check HSN in e-invoice vs item master.
expected_result: Consistent supply type and tax treatment across e-invoice, books and GSTR-1.
exception_conditions: Export under LUT coded EXPWP; SEZ supplies coded B2B; wrong POS.
exposure_basis: Refund rejection and table mismatches; potential output tax on mis-coded supplies.
corrective_action: Correct mapping in ERP e-invoice integration.

title: Outward e-way bills vs sales register
objective: Reconcile e-way bills generated against outward invoices to detect unreported supplies, value mismatches and EWBs without invoices.
procedure:
1. Download outward e-way bills (generated by the company and by transporters on its GSTIN) for the period.
2. Match EWB document number/date/value/GSTIN with sales register and stock transfer invoices.
3. Classify: EWB without invoice in books, invoice above threshold without EWB, value/HSN/quantity mismatch, GSTIN mismatch.
4. Investigate EWBs without corresponding sales (potential unrecorded supplies).
expected_result: Every active EWB maps to a booked document with consistent value and recipient.
exception_conditions: Active EWBs with no invoice in books; taxable value in EWB higher than invoice; recipient GSTIN differs.
exposure_basis: Short-paid output tax + interest u/s 50(1) @ 18% p.a. from the due date of the GSTR-3B of the original period to date of payment; penalty u/s 73/74 (periods up to FY 2023-24) or u/s 74A (FY 2024-25 onwards) if raised in proceedings. Unreconciled active EWBs are a common basis for demand in scrutiny.
corrective_action: Account for unrecorded supplies with tax and interest, cancel erroneous EWBs within time, and integrate EWB generation with the invoicing system.

title: Consignments above Rs 50,000 moved without e-way bill
objective: Identify outward and inward movements exceeding the Rs 50,000 consignment value threshold without an e-way bill.
procedure:
1. Filter goods invoices, stock transfers and delivery challans with consignment value (including tax) above Rs 50,000 (or lower State threshold for intra-State where applicable).
2. Exclude exempt goods/movements under Rule 138(14) and non-motorised conveyance cases with documentation.
3. Match with EWB register; list documents without EWB.
4. Review transporter-generated EWBs before concluding exception.
expected_result: EWB available for every movement exceeding threshold.
exception_conditions: Stock transfers and job work dispatches without EWB; customer pickups without EWB.
exposure_basis: Detention/penalty u/s 129 (200% of tax payable for taxable goods where owner comes forward, as amended w.e.f. 01.01.2022) on interception; penalty u/s 122 for transport without documents; reputational and supply-chain disruption.
corrective_action: Implement hard stop on dispatch without EWB, train logistics on Rule 138(14) exemptions.

title: Tax amounts entered in cess field of e-way bills
objective: Detect e-way bills where GST amounts are captured in the cess field (or vice versa), causing mismatches with invoices and returns.
procedure:
1. Extract EWB tax fields (CGST, SGST, IGST, cess, cess non-advol).
2. Flag EWBs where cess is non-zero for HSNs not attracting cess, or where cess equals the expected GST and GST fields are zero.
3. Compare with invoice tax breakup.
4. Identify the source (manual entry, integration mapping).
expected_result: EWB tax fields mirror invoice tax heads.
exception_conditions: GST captured as cess; IGST captured in CGST/SGST fields.
exposure_basis: Mismatch-driven scrutiny and transit detention risk on document discrepancies (generally minor penalty if no evasion intent).
corrective_action: Fix integration mapping and update EWB within allowed window or cancel and regenerate.

title: Cancelled, rejected or discarded e-way bills where goods actually moved or invoice booked
objective: Identify EWBs cancelled within 24 hours or rejected by recipient while the related invoice remains in books and goods moved.
procedure:
1. Extract cancelled and rejected EWBs with reasons.
2. Match document numbers with sales register and GSTR-1.
3. Where invoice remains active, verify whether a replacement EWB was generated for the movement.
4. Investigate patterns of repeated cancellation for the same customer/vehicle.
expected_result: Cancelled EWBs relate to cancelled supplies or replaced by valid EWB.
exception_conditions: Invoice booked but EWB cancelled with no replacement; frequent cancellations post movement.
exposure_basis: Detention/penalty u/s 129 (200% of tax payable for taxable goods where owner comes forward, as amended w.e.f. 01.01.2022) on interception; penalty u/s 122 for transport without documents; reputational and supply-chain disruption.
corrective_action: Generate valid EWB process controls and investigate anomalies; document reasons for cancellations.

title: Bill-from / dispatch-from address mismatch with registered places of business
objective: Ensure dispatch-from addresses on EWBs are registered places of business of the GSTIN and that bill-from GSTIN corresponds to the State of dispatch.
procedure:
1. Extract dispatch-from PIN code and address from EWBs.
2. Compare with registered principal and additional places of business.
3. Identify dispatches from third-party warehouses or other State locations under a different GSTIN.
4. For bill-from-dispatch-from transactions (Type 3/4), verify supporting documents.
expected_result: All dispatch locations registered and consistent with bill-from GSTIN.
exception_conditions: Goods dispatched from unregistered warehouses; dispatch State differs from GSTIN State without valid bill-from-dispatch-from structure.
exposure_basis: Detention/penalty u/s 129 (200% of tax payable for taxable goods where owner comes forward, as amended w.e.f. 01.01.2022) on interception; penalty u/s 122 for transport without documents; reputational and supply-chain disruption. Also registration non-compliance (see A-REG-001).
corrective_action: Register locations, correct EWB templates, and validate dispatch PIN in ERP.

title: Inward e-way bills generated on company GSTIN vs purchase register
objective: Use inward EWBs as evidence of receipt and to detect purchases not booked or EWBs raised on the company without supply.
procedure:
1. Download EWBs generated by others where the company is recipient.
2. Match with purchase register and GRNs.
3. List inward EWBs without purchase booking and invoices without EWBs where required.
4. Reject EWBs not relating to the company within 72 hours going forward.
expected_result: Inward EWBs reconcile to purchases.
exception_conditions: Inward EWBs unrelated to genuine purchases (misuse of GSTIN); purchases without EWB.
exposure_basis: Potential ITC challenge where receipt cannot be evidenced; misuse of GSTIN by third parties.
corrective_action: Reject unrelated EWBs, follow up vendors, and investigate GSTIN misuse.

title: E-way bills for job work, stock transfer, FOC and returns on delivery challan
objective: Ensure movements other than sales (job work, branch transfer, FOC, sale-on-approval, returns) are covered by delivery challans and EWBs.
procedure:
1. Extract non-sale stock movements from the stock register.
2. Verify delivery challans issued with prescribed particulars.
3. Verify EWB generated where required (job work inter-State movements require EWB irrespective of value).
4. Match job work challans with ITC-04.
expected_result: All non-sale movements documented with challans and EWBs.
exception_conditions: Job work dispatches without EWB; returns from customers without documents.
